conviction_note: The evidence leans mildly positive: Citi's Securities Services rose 4% QoQ with NII up 7% QoQ, and State Street's own September update raised the fee guide. But the consensus ($3.63 EPS, $4.04B revenue, $3.20B fees, $858M NII) already sits on the CFO's 'Q3 stable vs Q2' remark, and this name has sold 5 of its last 7 prints, including a -0.5% on the July beat-and-raise. So p_up is 52 on a 4.5% absolute move (implied 4.67%). That gives +0.18, against a findings sum of +0.8; the gap is the reaction function vetoing a modest fundamental beat.

findings.finding: At Barclays on 2026-09-14, CFO John Woods raised the FY26 fee revenue guide to +13-14% (from +12-13%) and put NII at the upper end of +14-15%. He called Q3 'stable vs Q2' across fees, NII and expenses, said servicing and management fees were running better than modelled while markets businesses moderated, and said expenses would be 'slightly higher'. Q3 consensus already sits on this: fees $3.20B vs about $3.19B in Q2, NII $858M vs $860M. The print lands inside what the company guided; the upside is only in the 'better than modelled' servicing and management fees.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026 beat ($3.65 vs $3.34, revenue $4.05B vs $3.88B) and full-year raise: -0.50% (baseline). 5 of the last 7 prints fell; January 2026 -6.07% and July 2025 -7.29% (lines not identified).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It was public intra-quarter guidance and consensus EPS moved up 0.6% in 30 days. If the market had also priced the 'better than modelled' servicing and management fees, consensus fees would sit above the Q2 run-rate rather than flat on it ($3.20B vs about $3.19B). The stock fell about 7% after the raise, so the guide raise bought nothing on the tape.
findings.independence: Peer read-through in finding 2 points the same way (Citi Securities Services +4% QoQ). Same-document caveat: the 'slightly higher' expense guide and the 'moderation in markets' remark come from this same transcript and are netted into this size, not filed separately.

findings.finding: Citi's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-13, after State Street last spoke) shows Securities Services revenue $1,712M, +13% YoY and +4% QoQ. NII was +7% QoQ ($801M vs $750M) and non-interest revenue +2% QoQ ($911M vs $893M), on AUC/A up 16% YoY. Services average deposits were +2% QoQ, and Markets FX revenue grew on higher volumes. A direct custody peer therefore grew sequentially in fees and NII, while State Street's consensus is flat QoQ on both (fees $3.20B vs about $3.19B, NII $858M vs $860M). JPM's same-day release shows deposits +2% QoQ and NII +6% QoQ firmwide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: State Street's NII and servicing-fee beats in Q2 2026 bought -0.5%. The baseline shows only 2 of 7 prints up, so line-level beats have not been paid.
findings.why_not_priced: It was released this morning, the day before State Street's print. The Zacks key-metric estimates (2026-10-09) predate it and show flat QoQ servicing fees and NII. If priced, State Street would have outperformed today and consensus NII would sit above Q2's $860M. Citi's own stock slipped on its beat (Investing.com headline), so sector tape does not show the read-through being bid.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, not State Street's number: Citi's mix is more deposit- and payments-heavy. JPM's 8-K (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/JPM/8-k-jpmorgan-chase-co-reports-material-event-6f03387f3670.html), with deposits +2% QoQ and NII +6% QoQ, is a second, broader peer pointing the same way. State Street's CFO said 'stable' on 2026-09-14 (finding 1), which caps the read-through.

findings.finding: Into the print the stock fell -6.79% over 20 sessions to $172.56, 11.2% below its 52w high and well below its 50-day MA of about $186. Over the same 30 days, Q3 consensus EPS rose 0.6% to $3.63 and the company raised its fee guide. That is a de-rating with rising estimates. The only sell-side moves found were target trims (BMO 212->200, Truist 191->190) with ratings kept, and there was no company-specific negative news.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026 came into the print near highs after a run-up and fell -0.5% on a beat (the Investing.com call note attributes the muted move to the prior run-up and to expense concerns). This time the setup is the reverse: a lower starting point.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly the opposite of unpriced: the drawdown IS the price. The claim is that the bar for the reaction is lower than in July. If the market were pricing a weak quarter, consensus would have been cut rather than raised 0.6%, and skew would be put-bid rather than -0.22.
findings.independence: Consensus revision from Zacks via Yahoo (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ahead-state-street-stt-q3-121501904.html). The cause of the drawdown is unidentified (the absence of an explanation is worth little by itself), so this is sized small.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call State Street flagged about $500M of mostly severance-related one-time costs for its transformation programme. Q1 2026 carried an $89M repositioning charge and Q2 none (10-Q). A further notable charge could land in Q3 or Q4 and would hit GAAP EPS against a $3.63 consensus that most previews treat ex-notables.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved instance found of State Street's reaction to a repositioning charge alone; the market has usually framed results ex-notable items.
findings.why_not_priced: Its timing is unknown. If a Q3 charge were expected, previews would show a GAAP vs ex-notable EPS split for Q3. None found does, and the Zacks consensus is a single $3.63.
findings.independence: The Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000093751/000009375126000397/stt-20260630.htm) shows $89M of six-month repositioning charges, all in Q1, so the bulk of the flagged cost is still to come. That is the same programme as this finding, not independent evidence.

findings.finding: The inputs to State Street Investment Management's fees were mixed in Q3. The S&P 500 gained about 2% in Q3 (narrow breadth), and SPY took $22.4B of inflows in the week to 2026-09-25 and $7.7B in the week to 2026-08-21. But global gold ETF AUM fell 7% m/m in September as gold declined, and GLD had outflows in the two most recent weeks. Consensus management fees are $812M vs $772M in Q2 (+5% QoQ), on AUM of $6.375T vs $6.3T at June 30.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 management fees were +29% YoY with $114B of net inflows; the stock reaction was -0.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Weekly flow prints are public; this is a proxy the street models. If analysts had read strong SPY inflows as decisive, consensus AUM would sit well above $6.375T.
findings.independence: The S&P Q3 return is from First Citizens' Q3 review (https://www.firstcitizens.com/content/dam/firstcitizens/pdfs/wealth/market-outlook/2026/q3-2026-quarterly-market-review.pdf), and the gold ETF data is the World Gold Council figure via search, pointing the other way. The two net to near zero.

findings.finding: The 8-K of 2026-09-14 (Item 5.02) moved Enterprise COO Mostapha Tahiri to a new role as President of State Street Alpha (Alpha, Charles River, platform solutions), with Ann Fogarty becoming Enterprise COO. Consensus software services revenue is $171M vs $227M a year ago, so the leadership change lands on the one fee line expected to shrink.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None found; software and processing revenue has rarely been the line State Street trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public 8-K. It is unpriced only to the extent the call reveals why Alpha needed a dedicated president; if an Alpha problem were priced, previews would be flagging Alpha bookings, and none found do.
findings.independence: Zacks key-metric table (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ahead-state-street-stt-q3-121501904.html): software services $170.68M vs $227M a year ago.

lessons_applied: Rule 1 and Rule 6: finding 1 (the Barclays guide) lands inside what the company guided and this name sells beats, so it went from +0.5 to +0.3
Rule 1 and Rule 5: finding 2 (the Citi Securities Services read-through) is a peer proxy that State Street's own 'stable' comment caps, so it went from +0.6 to +0.4
Rule 5: finding 3 (the drawdown with rising estimates) partly rests on the absence of an explanation, so it went from +0.5 to +0.2
Rule 2: finding 4 (the repositioning charge) is a one-off below the line with no path to the guide, so it went from -0.2 to -0.1
